evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'I'd love to help you with that. Let me kind of get some things set up here for you, so I can make sure that I get the accurate like rate and quote and all those good things.' — no time-boxed framing, no dependable quote promise, no wait for a yes before moving into probing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name: 'Allen... Quinton'; Move date: 'Monday... or Tuesday'; Route: 'Azel to Springtown'; Size: '700 square feet... about 900 square feet' — all four covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight into logistics probing after initial setup.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment, assisted living), floor (first floor, no stairs), rooms/size (700 sq ft → 900 sq ft), walking distance (ten minutes apart), special items (bookcases, dresser with mirror, recliners, bed, TV console, grandfather clock, curio cabinet, kitchen table, task chair, bedside tables, sofa table), box count (approximately 60).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Rep does not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'Approximately how many boxes would you say?' Customer: 'Probably sixteen we're gonna say approximately sixty.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides range: 'I do have a duration estimate of four to five hours. So call what that looks like cost wise would be that $966 to $1,160' and personalizes: 'we have a minimum of two and a half but let's just say we only utilize let's say three to four hours then you would be looking at a range of like, $772 to $820.' Includes trip fee ($190), hourly rate ($194 for two movers), wrapping/padding, disassembly/reassembly, 2.5-hour minimum.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed: '$190... already included'; hourly rate: '$194 that does include two movers'; 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments: 'anything over the two and a half hour minimum, we just... pro ran it fifteen minute increments... based off the time used.' No deposit: 'there is no deposit to book anything the truck is free to reserve. You don't pay for anything until after the move is completed.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly from estimate to 'Did you want to go ahead and get on the schedule?' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent, and without holding silence.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Two Promises section is skipped entirely.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway version: 'did you have any just general questions or concerns that I can answer after going through these things?' Customer says no concerns. Rep does not ask the genuine version 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Not asked. Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full: 'Did you want to go ahead and get on the schedule?' Asked plainly with no built-in out. Customer accepts: 'Yes.' Rep confirms: 'Okay, alrighty. Okay, I do have that reserved for you now.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes: 'there is no deposit to book anything the truck is free to reserve. You don't pay for anything until after the move is completed.'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date: Monday, September 28th confirmed. Time window: 8:00–8:30 confirmed. Addresses: 113 Denver Trail, Azel 76020 → 1203 J. Bird Lane, Springtown confirmed. Phone: Confirmed (Kathy's number on file). Crew size: Not explicitly confirmed (two movers mentioned in rate, not re-confirmed at booking). Notes: Yes, detailed parking/loading dock instructions added to notes, driver will call on arrival.

top_strength: Excellent logistics discovery and detail gathering — the rep captured all furniture items, box count, floor layout, parking logistics, and special access considerations in natural conversation, creating a strong foundation for a smooth move.
coaching_note: Critical gaps: skip Section 2 (Their Agenda / Two Layers Deep) entirely, bypass Section 5 (Two Promises) completely, and never ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate — these are load-bearing discovery and commitment-building sections that qualify the customer and reduce post-booking surprises; add them back into your flow before moving to the ask.
